newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Honeywell aims at US$200 mln Asia market.
newsitem.headline: Honeywell aims at US$200 mln Asia market.

text.p: Manufacturing control systems maker Honeywell Inc wants to tap the US$200 million hybrid control market in the Asia Pacific region, a company executive said on Monday.

"Honeywell is targeting the hybrid segment of the industrial manufacturing markets in the Asia Pacific," said Sam Hawkins, president of Honeywell Asia Pacific Inc, who told a news conference the market was worth around $200 million a year.
Hawkins said hybrid control systems, which regulate multiple maunfacturing processes, would "play a crucial role in Honeywell's future growth in the Asia Pacific region".
The hybrid control market was expected to double in value between now and the turn of the century, with demand led by China, Hawkins said.
"In China, there are hundreds of smaller power plants and chemical plants using old, outdated control equipment," he added.
Honeywell, which had worldwide sales of US$7.3 billion in 1996, sees potential in industries such as oil and gas and mining, Hawkins said.
